disclaimer: Use these contacts only in the country shown. Numbers and availability can change. In immediate danger, follow local authorities and the call operator. Administrative and Red Cross lines are not substitutes for emergency dispatch.

countries.name: International fallback
countries.callingNote: No emergency number works worldwide. 112 is guaranteed throughout the European Union; 911 is the primary number in the United States and some other countries. Verify locally before relying on either.

numbers.label: European Union emergency number
numbers.note: Free throughout the EU. It is not guaranteed worldwide.

numbers.label: United States emergency number
numbers.note: Primary emergency number in the United States; availability elsewhere varies.

organizations.name: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
organizations.note: Find the Red Cross or Red Crescent society serving your current country.

organizations.name: Restoring Family Links
organizations.note: International Red Cross and Red Crescent service for families separated by conflict, disaster or migration.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.callingNote: 123 is Colombia's free national single emergency line, available around the clock. Use it for real emergencies only.

numbers.label: National emergency line
numbers.note: Primary option for police, medical, fire and other state emergency services.

numbers.label: Police
numbers.note: National short code; territorial routing can vary. Prefer 123 when available.

numbers.label: Fire service
numbers.note: National short code; territorial routing can vary. Prefer 123 when available.

numbers.label: Ambulance
numbers.note: National short code; territorial routing can vary. Prefer 123 when available.

numbers.label: Colombian Red Cross emergency line
numbers.note: National allocation; operational availability can vary by territory. Use 123 for immediate dispatch.

organizations.name: Unidad Nacional para la Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres (UNGRD)
organizations.note: National disaster-risk information and citizen service, Monday to Friday; not an emergency dispatch line.

organizations.name: Cruz Roja Colombiana
organizations.note: National humanitarian assistance and information line; call 123 first for immediate danger.

organizations.name: Cruz Roja Colombiana — Restoring Family Links
organizations.note: WhatsApp channel for loss of family contact in humanitarian emergencies.

organizations.name: Fiscalía General de la Nación — Mecanismo de Búsqueda Urgente
organizations.note: Report a disappearance immediately, without waiting. From a landline call 01 8000 919748.

countries.name: United States
countries.callingNote: 911 is for immediate police, fire or medical emergencies. Dispatch is local.

numbers.label: Emergency services
numbers.note: Police, fire and ambulance for immediate danger.

organizations.name: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
organizations.note: Disaster assistance and recovery information; not emergency dispatch.

organizations.name: American Red Cross
organizations.note: Disaster assistance, shelter information and Red Cross services.

organizations.name: National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs)
organizations.note: Official national missing-person resource. Report first to 911 or local law enforcement; NamUs requires an active police report.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.callingNote: 911 is Mexico's single national emergency number and routes police, medical, fire, Civil Protection and Red Cross assistance.

numbers.label: National emergency number
numbers.note: Free, 24 hours a day, for real emergencies.

organizations.name: Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil
organizations.note: Official national civil-protection information; use 911 for immediate response.

organizations.name: Cruz Roja Mexicana
organizations.note: Administrative headquarters, not emergency dispatch. Emergencies are routed through 911 or a local delegation.

organizations.name: Comisión Nacional de Búsqueda
organizations.note: Report a disappearance immediately; the official line operates 24/7.

countries.name: Spain
countries.callingNote: 112 is free and covers every emergency type throughout Spain, including from locked phones or phones without an active SIM where technically available.

numbers.label: Single emergency number
numbers.note: Police, ambulance, fire and rescue throughout Spain.

numbers.label: National Police
numbers.note: Urgent National Police assistance.

numbers.label: Guardia Civil
numbers.note: Urgent Guardia Civil assistance.

organizations.name: Dirección General de Protección Civil y Emergencias
organizations.note: Administrative information and national civil-protection guidance; not emergency dispatch.

organizations.name: Cruz Roja Española
organizations.note: Free information and assistance line during published service hours; use 112 for immediate danger.

organizations.name: Centro Nacional de Desaparecidos (CNDES)
organizations.note: Report a disappearance immediately through 091, 062 or in person; there is no 24-hour waiting period.

countries.name: Germany
countries.callingNote: 112 reaches fire and medical rescue; 110 reaches police. Both are free emergency calls.

numbers.label: Fire and medical rescue
numbers.note: Life-threatening medical emergencies, fire and rescue.

numbers.label: Police
numbers.note: Immediate police assistance.

organizations.name: Bundesamt für Bevölkerungsschutz und Katastrophenhilfe (BBK)
organizations.note: Federal civil-protection and disaster-preparedness information.

organizations.name: Deutsches Rotes Kreuz (DRK)
organizations.note: German Red Cross humanitarian services; use 112 for immediate danger.

organizations.name: DRK-Suchdienst
organizations.note: Tracing service for families separated by conflict, migration or disaster.

countries.name: France
countries.callingNote: 112 routes any emergency. France also keeps service-specific national numbers.

numbers.label: European emergency number
numbers.note: Routes to the appropriate emergency service.

numbers.label: SAMU medical emergency
numbers.note: Urgent medical assistance.

numbers.label: Police secours
numbers.note: Immediate police or gendarmerie assistance.

numbers.label: Fire and rescue
numbers.note: Firefighters and rescue.

numbers.label: Missing children
numbers.note: European hotline for a missing child; call 17 or 112 if danger is immediate.

organizations.name: Direction générale de la sécurité civile et de la gestion des crises
organizations.note: Official civil-security information; no public national dispatch phone is published.

organizations.name: Croix-Rouge française
organizations.note: National administrative contact, not emergency dispatch. Use 112, 15, 17 or 18 for immediate danger.

organizations.name: 116 000 Enfants Disparus
organizations.note: Officially recognized support hotline for families of missing children.

countries.name: China
countries.callingNote: Mainland China uses separate emergency numbers. There is no single nationwide 911/112 equivalent.

numbers.label: Police
numbers.note: Crime, personal danger and urgent police assistance.

numbers.label: Fire and rescue
numbers.note: Fire and rescue incidents.

numbers.label: Medical ambulance
numbers.note: Emergency medical and ambulance dispatch.

organizations.name: 中华人民共和国应急管理部 (Ministry of Emergency Management)
organizations.note: National emergency-management information; use the service numbers above for immediate help.

organizations.name: 中国红十字会总会 (Red Cross Society of China)
organizations.note: Administrative inquiries on working days, not emergency dispatch.

countries.name: Japan
countries.callingNote: 110 reaches police; 119 reaches fire and ambulance anywhere in Japan.

numbers.label: Police
numbers.note: Crime, traffic accidents and immediate police assistance.

numbers.label: Fire and ambulance
numbers.note: State whether you need fire service or an ambulance.

organizations.name: 内閣府 防災情報 (Cabinet Office Disaster Management)
organizations.note: National disaster information and multilingual preparedness resources; not emergency dispatch.

organizations.name: 日本赤十字社 (Japanese Red Cross Society)
organizations.note: General headquarters contact and humanitarian information; use 110 or 119 for immediate danger.

organizations.name: Japanese Red Cross — family contact after disasters
organizations.note: Guidance points affected families to the responsible prefecture and local authorities; urgent cases go to police on 110.
